title: RunSet
description: An evaluation over more than one resource, exactly as `RunSet.to_dict()` emits it. A directory is a stable input shape whether it holds one document today and fifty tomorrow, so its result is an envelope rather than a bare list. Described as it is: two field names disagree with the Run envelope and that is recorded here rather than corrected.

resources.description: How many resources were observed. It cannot say how many the identity failed to return, and `run_coverage` is where that limit is recorded rather than inferred.

by_class.description: Resource class to how many carried it. A label, never a filter.

set_aside.description: How many runs a profile moved BELOW THE FOLD. Not how many were skipped: their findings are evaluated, counted and printed, just lower down. This said 'set aside rather than evaluated', which is the opposite of what the engine does, and a consumer implementing the contract as written would report evaluated resources as unevaluated.

run_coverage.description: The same idea a Run calls `coverage`, under a different name. `expected` is deliberately optional here: counting documents proves how many resources were observed and never how many were missed, so its absence is stored as not-established rather than as complete coverage.

runs.description: Each run whole. Duplicate resource ids are refused at construction, because two documents describing one resource is a collection defect and not a set of two.

$schema.description: The exact contract this document claims, which must be the $id of the schema validating it. An instance convention and not the dialect keyword: inside a schema document `$schema` names the JSON Schema dialect, and using one field for both meanings is what this separation exists to prevent. It replaces `schema_version`, which was a second version that could not even express the one in the $id — `1.0` against a contract ending in `/1.2.0` — and was maintained by hand.

services.description:
WHAT WAS OBSERVED, BY SERVICE AND BY AREA, so a consumer opens a result and sees which parts of Microsoft 365 were looked at before it sees a rule identifier. A reader was shown findings grouped by whatever the interface chose, which describes this engine's internals rather than their tenant.

PUBLISHED RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE COMPUTED. A consumer deriving this would be a second authority on what a service is and what an area is, and the first thing it would disagree about is a service that collected evidence and reached no conclusion.

NO PERCENTAGE IS DERIVABLE FROM THIS AND NONE IS INTENDED. `conclusions` is a count of conclusions, never a numerator: the denominator would be the number of questions somebody could have asked, which nobody knows, and `D5` forbids the aggregate that would produce.

service.description: The workload the evidence names, never a label chosen here.

state.description: THE WEAKEST AREA THIS SERVICE HAS. Reporting the strongest would be the aggregate this product refuses, in the place a reader looks first: a service that read four things and could not read one is not observed.

conclusions.description: Results that decided something, counted in the area they were decided FROM. A rule reading two areas counts in both, because picking one would be tidiness asserted as fact.

unresolved.description: Results that are `unknown` or `invalid-evidence`. Kept apart from conclusions because a rule that could not decide is not a rule that decided nothing is wrong.

areas.description: What the collector declared it requested, and how far each reading got.

state.description: `not-observed` is a reading nobody made; `refused` is one the tenant or this product declined; `partial` is one that returned some of what it covers. Three states that look alike on a screen and are not the same, and a product collapsing them describes a collector that never ran exactly as one that ran and could not answer.

population.description: How many documents contributed to this area. A count, never the things counted.

acquisition.description: The collectors whose documents fed this area, from their own provenance.

detail.description: WHY, IN THE COLLECTOR'S WORDS, where it gave a reason. A state without one tells a reader that something is partial and not WHAT part, which is the shape of a status nobody can act on. Null where the reading succeeded and there was nothing to explain.

observed_at.description: When this area was last read. A reading is true of a moment, and an artefact opened a year later describes the tenant of that day. The LATEST of the documents that fed it, because what a reader wants is how current this is rather than when it first happened.
